notes.title: Classic '90s shooter may return to life after dev drops source code
notes.notes:
Early shooters were easy to get lost in but none were more confusingly laid out than the original Descent games. Navigating your spaceship through fully 3D spaces in a series of labyrinthine asteroid mines led many to desperation, lost in an endless series of caverns trying to find the missing miners they needed to rescue in order to make their escape. In 1999, Descent 3 launched, revolutionizing the series by allowing players the ability to leave the mines behind for the first time, blasting enemy robots while jetting around above ground.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Descent 3 has been made open source
notes.notes:
Another classic has been given the open source treatment, with Descent 3 from Outrage Entertainment now available under the MIT license.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2024/04/descent-3-has-been-made-open-source

notes.title: Building a Retro Linux Gaming Computer - Part 4: Installing Red Hat Linux 7.3
notes.notes:
I had some grief installing Red Hat Linux 7.3 but with persistence I was able to get it installed. In terms of compatibility though Valhalla proved to be far superior, so I decided to stick with it and focus on improving other parts of the system instead.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2021/03/building-a-retro-linux-gaming-computer-part-4-installing-red-hat-linux-73

notes.title: Building a Retro Linux Gaming Computer - Part 3: Installing Red Hat Linux 9
notes.notes:
My first choice was to run Red Hat Linux 9, for the arbitrary reason that it was the final release of the once dominant distribution and the second to feature the delightful Bluecurve desktop theme for both Gnome and KDE. I knew then that I was cutting things a bit close, but I still found myself disappointed with the outcome.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2021/03/building-a-retro-linux-gaming-computer-part-3-installing-red-hat-linux-9
